name: discrete_gate
purpose: Experimental candidate filter in the context of the Beal conjecture (not a solver or proof) performing deterministic preliminary screening under specified conditions.

numbers.constraints: len >= 1 (This is the behavior of the current implementation. Its mathematical justification and correspondence to the primary source have not been confirmed; triads canonical), all elements > 0, strict int (no bool, no float)

exponents.constraints: len == len(numbers), all elements >= 1, strict int (no bool, no float)

threshold.constraints: finite float > 0.0, no NaN, no inf, no bool

algorithm.step_1: Strict precondition and type validation on raw inputs
algorithm.step_3: Calculate dmod = round((sum(exponents) / 100.0) + (0.0 if source_present else 1.0), 10)
algorithm.step_4: If check_exponent_limit and min(exponents) <= 2 -> VOID (reason: EXPONENT_LIMIT_EXCLUSION)

guarantees: Zero runtime external dependencies (Python standard library only)
Defensive input immutability via frozen tuples
Preservation of mathematical diagnostics in VOID results
limitations: NOT a Diophantine equation solver (PASS indicates that the candidate passed the checks of this filter; by itself, this result does not prove numerical equality, the existence of a solution, or the truth of a theorem)
Early screening tool: Performance was not measured; the impact of the filter on execution time and operation count is unknown
source_faithful mode is locked until authentic Zenodo listing is ingested

epistemic_status.dmod_formula: REPORTED (scaling /100 and tamas penalty are implementation choices not verified in primary source)
epistemic_status.branch_priority_order: PROJECT_PROPOSAL (exponent limit check <= 2 evaluated prior to gcd check)
